steps.because: so the whole of it is the long-range law times one plus a correction. The one is what becomes Newton's inverse square; the correction is the middle's logarithm over the long-range term, and it carries \bar{c}/R - worth per cent at a few cells and nothing at all once R is an astronomical number of lattice steps

there is a core at each end and they are the same by symmetry. Added to the inverse-square part of the middle, the (R - \bar{c}) that each carries cancels over a common denominator - which is what makes the long-range law a plain power of R with no trace of the core size left in its exponent
met_{far} is not a primitive of this theory - it is 2·one core, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
the correction is what the middle's tail is worth against the long-range law - a ratio of the two, and the thing that goes to nothing as R grows

the middle runs from the edge of one core to the edge of the other, and one over x integrated between them is a logarithm - which grows more slowly than any power, and is the whole of why the correction dies away

between the two cores the integrand is a genuine product of two falling densities. By partial fractions that splits into a part carrying the same power of the separation as the cores do - which sums with them - and this part, one power of R further down and going as one over the distance along the line. It is the second that gives the correction, and being a power lower is exactly why the correction shrinks as the bodies are moved apart
the middle's tail goes as one over x, whose integral is a logarithm - so between \bar{c} and R it is ln(R/\bar{c}). It grows more slowly than any power of x, which is what matters about it here
the middle is \frac{ln(R/\bar{c})}{R^{D}} and met_{far} is 2·one core, so the one over the other is 1/2·\frac{\bar{c}^{D-2}·ln(R/\bar{c})}{R}
near is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1/2·\frac{\bar{c}^{D-2}·ln(R/\bar{c})}{R}, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the correction is what the middle's tail is worth against the long-range law - a ratio of the two, and the thing that goes to nothing as R grows

the middle runs from the edge of one core to the edge of the other, and one over x integrated between them is a logarithm - which grows more slowly than any power, and is the whole of why the correction dies away
